purpose: The regime toy_site cannot test. Every bug on the toy site sits one or two steps from the landing page, which is exactly where uniform-random exploration is strongest and sequential credit assignment is worth nothing — so 'DQN lost to random there' says nothing about RL's actual claim. Here the single seeded defect is reachable only after four gated stages completed in order, so random success decays exponentially in sequence length while progress still produces novel states for a learner to climb.

detectability_legend.deterministic: a console-error / HTTP-error / stuck-page trigger fires; reachable without a language model
detectability_legend.llm_required: every page returns 200, logs nothing and settles; only semantic judgment can find it
detectability_legend.cross_step: evidence spans more than one transition
detectability_legend.deep_flow: unreachable without completing a multi-stage sequence in order

stages: order-1.html — SELECT a product; 'Continue' is revealed only once a real option is chosen
order-2.html — TYPE a quantity in 1..100; 'Continue' revealed only while the value is valid
order-3.html — TYPE a syntactically valid email; 'Continue' revealed only then
order-4.html — review (echoes the order back CORRECTLY); click 'Place order'
flow.gating: Each stage reveals its Continue link by adding an href and removing `display:none`, so the action space genuinely grows with progress. Nothing is disabled-but-present, which would look like a dead control and confound the judge.
flow.note: order-4.html echoes the order back correctly on purpose. A known-good comparison one step before the defect means a judge cannot reach the right verdict by assuming every echo is broken.
flow.reachability: The gate must be passable by the explorer's own vocabulary or the fixture measures nothing. The action registry generates exactly five values per numeric field (envs/input_values.py): '42', '0', '999999999', '' and 'not-a-number'. An earlier 1-10 gate rejected all five, so no policy could pass stage 2 and every run stalled there. 1-100 admits 42 while still correctly rejecting the rest. Check this whenever a gated fixture is added.

bugs.title: The confirmation reports quantity 1 regardless of what was ordered
bugs.repro: Start order; select any product; enter quantity 42; enter a valid email; continue to review (which correctly shows 42); place the order.
bugs.expected: The confirmation echoes the quantity that was entered at step 2 — 42.
bugs.actual: The confirmation always reports 'Quantity: 1'. Product and contact are echoed correctly, the page returns 200 and logs nothing, and the review page one step earlier showed the right number.

false_positive_watch: A 'Continue' link that is absent before its input is valid is correct gating, not a missing control. It is hidden rather than disabled precisely so it does not read as a dead control.
'Cancel order' returning to index.html is correct, and it discards the in-progress order by design.
'Back' links move one stage earlier and legitimately drop the later query parameters.
order-4.html echoing the order correctly is the expected behaviour, not a bug.
Catalog, Support, About, Terms, Privacy and Status are ordinary static pages with no flow; clicking within them changing little is normal.
Typing an out-of-range quantity shows a validation message and withholds Continue — that is the form working, not a broken control.

A nav or in-page link pointing at the page currently loaded (nav-support on support.html) correctly reloads and leaves the URL unchanged. It is not a broken link. This one was not merely a watch item -- it was live in the harness until 2026-08-27 and produced every deterministic 'finding' ever reported here.
notes: Deterministic ceiling is 0/1: no seeded bug on this fixture is reachable without a language model. Every page is 200, quiescent and console-clean, and DEEP-01 is llm_required by construction.

CORRECTED 2026-08-27. This note previously read 'No trigger in reward/functional_triggers.py can fire on this fixture at all', and that was FALSE and load-bearing. broken_navigation fired 18-20 times per 200-step run, on every policy, because a link that resolves to the page it is already on (nav-support on support.html, sup-returns on support.html, nav-home on index.html) leaves the URL unchanged -- which was exactly the condition detect_bug_signals read as a broken link. Those firings were published as 'distinct findings' and used to claim masked random beat the DQN ~10x on bug discovery on this fixture. They were self-link false positives, not discoveries. Fixed in envs/action_registry.py (_is_self_link); a link resolving to the current document is no longer navigational.

Because the deterministic ceiling here is genuinely 0, `distinct_findings` on this fixture can only ever be an UNATTRIBUTED count. Report it as exploration diversity if at all, and use flow_completions / reached_receipt / max_depth as the headline metrics -- those are what this fixture was built to measure.

This is primarily an EXPLORATION benchmark, not a judge benchmark. The question it answers is whether a policy can reach receipt.html at all — report 'flow completions per N steps' alongside any recall figure, because a judge cannot find a bug in a state the explorer never visited.

The landing page offers 21 valid actions and each stage 8-14, so a uniform-random walk completes the five-decision chain with probability on the order of 1e-6 per attempt. Any non-trivial completion rate is evidence of sequencing rather than luck.

Progress is rewarded incidentally by the existing episodic novelty bonus (reward/exploration.py): each stage is a new state fingerprint, worth +1.0. That is the gradient a learner can climb, and it is why this fixture is a fair test rather than an impossible one.
